The Netherlands built a 9-kilometer storm barrier, known as the Eastern Scheldt Barrier, to protect against floods while maintaining tidal flow. However, this engineering solution has disrupted natural sediment flows, leading to the phenomenon known as 'sand hunger', which is causing tidal flats and mudflats in the region to shrink. Authorities are implementing sand nourishment projects to address these environmental changes and preserve coastal ecosystems.

 - The Eastern Scheldt Barrier was constructed to provide flood protection while allowing for tidal exchange.
 - The barrier has resulted in erosion of tidal flats due to reduced sediment movement, prompting efforts to replenish these areas.

Source: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/netherlands-built-a-9-km-storm-barrier-to-protect-against-floods-decades-later-sand-hunger-began-shrinking-tidal-flats/articleshow/134049982.cms

Category: Geopolitics
Importance: 7
The Netherlands has implemented a 9-kilometer storm barrier to prevent flooding, a significant engineering feat completed in 1986. However, this barrier has led to an environmental issue known as 'sand hunger', where the reduced tidal currents have disrupted the natural sand movement, resulting in erosion of tidal flats and mudflats over the decades. To combat this, the Dutch authorities are now planning to nourish these areas with sand to maintain their ecological functions and protect against rising sea levels.

 - The Eastern Scheldt Barrier was constructed following the North Sea flood of 1953 to protect the region from flooding.
 - The barrier's impact on tidal currents has led to a significant ecological challenge known as 'sand hunger', necessitating interventions to restore sediment balance.

On September 11, 2001, the town of Gander in Canada accommodated around 7,000 stranded American passengers and crew after 38 planes were diverted there due to the US airspace closure following the 9/11 attacks. The local community provided food, shelter, and support during a time of crisis, showcasing significant hospitality despite the limited resources available in the small town. As of today, the events in Gander remain a lasting example of human kindness amid tragedy, contrasting with contemporary tensions in US-Canada relations.

 - Gander sheltered thousands of Americans during the 9/11 crisis after US airspace was closed.
 - Residents provided essential support to the stranded passengers, which became a significant part of the town's identity.
 - The story of Gander has been memorialized through various cultural expressions, including the musical 'Come From Away'.

Source: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/after-9/11-canadas-tiny-town-of-gander-sheltered-7000-americans-for-days-providing-food-and-refuge-as-38-planes-landed-there-following-the-attack/articleshow/134049375.cms
